classification.difficultyReason: Continue the all-determinable-angles task using reflex, right-angle and parallel constraints without inventing missing measurements.

content.prompt: Calculate as many angles as you can in these diagrams. You do not need to show reasoning.

spec.description: A, B and E are collinear, rising right. BC and ED descend vertically with matching upward parallel markers. The exterior major arc at E denotes the given reflex angle of 300 degrees.
spec.mathematics: BC parallel ED. Reflex BED = 300 degrees. Drawing coordinates use the implied 60-degree minor angle without adding a student-visible measurement.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 300-degree reflex angle is visible.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle BED&=360^\circ-300^\circ\\\angle BED&=60^\circ\end{align*}$$ Angles at a point.

$\angle ABC=60^\circ$ (corresponding angles on parallel lines).

$$\begin{align*}\angle CBE&=180^\circ-60^\circ\\\angle CBE&=120^\circ\end{align*}$$ Angles on a straight line.

spec.description: A–B–E slopes down to the right. BC and ED descend vertically with upward parallel markers. EF extends right. The 150-degree label is above E; a right-angle square lies between ED and EF.
spec.mathematics: A, B, E collinear; BC parallel ED; BEF = 150 degrees; DEF = 90 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Given 150 degrees and right-angle marker only.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle BED+150^\circ+90^\circ&=360^\circ\\\angle BED+240^\circ&=360^\circ\\\angle BED&=120^\circ\end{align*}$$ Angles at a point.

$\angle ABC=120^\circ$ (corresponding angles on parallel lines).

$$\begin{align*}\angle CBE&=180^\circ-120^\circ\\\angle CBE&=60^\circ\end{align*}$$ Angles on a straight line.

spec.description: A–B–C–D slopes down right. BF and CE extend only to the right, with matching rightward parallel markers. The given angle is ECD.
spec.mathematics: BF parallel CE; ECD = 65 degrees; A, B, C, D collinear.

answer.worked:
$\angle FBC=65^\circ$ (corresponding angles on parallel lines).

$$\begin{align*}\angle ABF&=180^\circ-65^\circ\\\angle ABF&=115^\circ\\\angle BCE&=180^\circ-65^\circ\\\angle BCE&=115^\circ\end{align*}$$ Angles on a straight line.

spec.description: Triangle BCD, with B left, D upper right and C lower right. BA points vertically upward; BA and CD have upward parallel markers. The 45-degree angle is between BA and BD; 75 degrees is inside at C.
spec.mathematics: BA parallel CD; ABD = 45 degrees; BCD = 75 degrees. Coordinates use B=(0,0), D=(1.5,1.5), C=(1.5,-1.5 tan 15 degrees).

answer.worked:
$\angle BDC=45^\circ$ (alternate angles on parallel lines).

$$\begin{align*}\angle ABC+75^\circ&=180^\circ\\\angle ABC&=105^\circ\end{align*}$$ Co-interior angles on parallel lines.

$$\begin{align*}\angle DBC&=105^\circ-45^\circ\\\angle DBC&=60^\circ\end{align*}$$ Adjacent angles.

spec.description: Vertical AB forms the left side of triangle ABD. DC extends vertically down from D. Upward parallel markers appear on AB and DC. Interior angles at A and D are 30 and 85 degrees.
spec.mathematics: AB parallel DC; BAD = 30 degrees; ADB = 85 degrees. D=(1.2,0), A=(0,1.2 tan 60 degrees), B=(0,-1.2 tan 25 degrees).

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle ADC+30^\circ&=180^\circ\\\angle ADC&=150^\circ\end{align*}$$ Co-interior angles on parallel lines.

$$\begin{align*}\angle BDC&=150^\circ-85^\circ\\\angle BDC&=65^\circ\end{align*}$$ Adjacent angles.

$\angle ABD=65^\circ$ (alternate angles on parallel lines).

spec.description: Inverted triangle ABD above horizontal C–D–E. AB and CE have matching rightward parallel markers. A right-angle square is inside ADB; 45 degrees is between DB and DE.
spec.mathematics: AB parallel CE; ADB = 90 degrees; BDE = 45 degrees. No equal-side marks.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied 45 degrees and right-angle square.

answer.worked:
$\angle ABD=45^\circ$ (alternate angles on parallel lines).

$$\begin{align*}\angle CDA+90^\circ+45^\circ&=180^\circ\\\angle CDA&=45^\circ\end{align*}$$ Angles on a straight line.

$\angle BAD=45^\circ$ (alternate angles on parallel lines).

$$\begin{align*}\angle CDB&=45^\circ+90^\circ\\\angle CDB&=135^\circ\\\angle ADE&=90^\circ+45^\circ\\\angle ADE&=135^\circ\end{align*}$$ Adjacent angles.

spec.description: Triangle ABD with horizontal base AB below horizontal E–D–C. Rightward parallel markers are on ED and AB. Interior DAB is 40 degrees; exterior BDC is 80 degrees.
spec.mathematics: AB parallel EC; DAB = 40 degrees; BDC = 80 degrees. Coordinates derive A and B from a common altitude and the printed angles.

answer.worked:
$\angle EDA=40^\circ$ and $\angle ABD=80^\circ$ (alternate angles on parallel lines).

$$\begin{align*}40^\circ+\angle ADB+80^\circ&=180^\circ\\\angle ADB&=60^\circ\end{align*}$$ Angles on the straight line $EDC$.

$$\begin{align*}\angle ADC&=60^\circ+80^\circ\\\angle ADC&=140^\circ\\\angle EDB&=40^\circ+60^\circ\\\angle EDB&=100^\circ\end{align*}$$ Adjacent angles.

spec.description: Triangle ABD has vertical AB left of vertical E–D–C. Matching upward markers indicate parallelism. The square at D is inside ADB; 35 degrees is inside ABD.
spec.mathematics: AB parallel EC; ADB = 90 degrees; ABD = 35 degrees. D=(1.4,0), A=(0,1.4 tan 35 degrees), B=(0,-1.4 tan 55 degrees).
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied 35 degrees and right-angle marker.

answer.worked:
$\angle BDC=35^\circ$ (alternate angles on parallel lines).

$$\begin{align*}\angle ADE+90^\circ+35^\circ&=180^\circ\\\angle ADE&=55^\circ\end{align*}$$ Angles on the straight line $EDC$.

$\angle BAD=55^\circ$ (alternate angles on parallel lines).

$$\begin{align*}\angle ADC&=90^\circ+35^\circ\\\angle ADC&=125^\circ\\\angle BDE&=90^\circ+55^\circ\\\angle BDE&=145^\circ\end{align*}$$ Adjacent angles.

spec.description: Hourglass formed by triangles ABC and EDC. AB is above ED; both carry rightward parallel markers. A–C–D and B–C–E are straight. The 25-degree label is at B. An unlabelled major arc at E marks reflex CED.
spec.mathematics: AB parallel ED; ABC = 25 degrees. The angle of the other diagonal is an unmeasured drawing parameter, not an additional given. No right-angle or equal-side marks.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 25 degrees is printed. The marked reflex angle at E remains unlabelled.

answer.worked:
$\angle CED=25^\circ$ (alternate angles on parallel lines).

$$\begin{align*}\text{reflex }\angle CED&=360^\circ-25^\circ\\\text{reflex }\angle CED&=335^\circ\end{align*}$$ Angles at a point.

The angles at $A$, $C$ and $D$ cannot be determined uniquely from the given information.
